PinCam

Privacy Policy

Effective 14 October 2026

PinCam in short

PinCam is a camera app that stamps your photos and videos with where and when they were taken. It is made by Butter Paper Labs.

PinCam has no accounts and no servers of its own. Your photos, videos and their locations stay on your phone unless you choose to share them. To draw the map, find the address and show the weather, PinCam asks a few outside services, described below. PinCam is free with ads, and only if you agree, it sends us crash reports and anonymous usage data.

What PinCam uses and why

  • Camera: to show the viewfinder, take photos and record videos.
  • Microphone: to record sound with your videos, only while you are recording one. It is asked for the first time you choose Video, and you can turn sound off in Preferences (Record sound). Sound stays in the video on your phone and is never sent anywhere. If you don’t allow it, videos are saved without sound.
  • Precise location: to stamp each photo and video with its address, coordinates and altitude, to save the location inside the file (a photo’s EXIF data, a video’s metadata), and to show the map and weather. Location is used only while PinCam is open on your screen, never in the background. If you don’t allow it, PinCam still works and saves photos and videos without a location.
  • Compass and motion sensors: to show which way the camera points and how you are holding the phone. These readings never leave your phone.
  • Photo library: to save your photos and videos in a "PinCam" album. PinCam does not read, upload or analyse the other photos or videos in your library. On iPhone it asks for full access only because Apple requires it to keep an album. If you choose a picture as your own logo for the stamp, your phone’s photo picker hands PinCam only that picture, and PinCam keeps a copy of it on your phone.
  • Network status: to notice when you are offline, so it can look up addresses later.

What stays on your phone

Your photos and videos, the list of them in PinCam’s gallery (file names, time, coordinates, altitude and address), your preferences and any logo you chose are stored only on your phone. They are never sent to us. We have no servers, so we could not see them even if we wanted to.

Services that receive some information

PinCam sends only what each feature needs, over encrypted connections (HTTPS):

  • Google Maps, by Google: the map on the viewfinder and on your photos. Google receives the area of the map being shown (around your location), your IP address and basic device information. Use of Google Maps features in PinCam is subject to the Google Maps Additional Terms of Service (maps.google.com/help/terms_maps) and the Google Privacy Policy (policies.google.com/privacy).
  • Address lookup: your phone’s built-in address service, run by Google on Android and by Apple on iPhone. It receives the coordinates of where you are (when you open the camera, then only after you move about 25 metres) and of photos still waiting for an address. See the Google Privacy Policy or the Apple Privacy Policy (apple.com/legal/privacy).
  • Weather: MET Norway, the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, and only while a weather detail is switched on in the stamp. It receives your location rounded to about 1 km, and your IP address, which it keeps in its traffic logs. See its privacy policy (met.no/en/About-us/privacy).
  • Ads, by Google AdMob: PinCam shows a banner in its gallery, and a short video ad when you choose to watch one to unlock a feature. Ads never appear on the camera. To show and measure ads, Google receives your phone’s advertising ID (on Android; on iPhone only if you allow tracking), your IP address and the approximate location it suggests, basic device information, and how you interact with the ads. It does not receive your photos, videos or where you took them. See how Google uses information from apps that use its services (policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites). You can reset or delete your advertising ID, or limit ad personalisation, in your phone’s settings.
  • Crash reports and usage data, by Google’s Firebase (Crashlytics and Google Analytics for Firebase), only if you choose "Share usage data" (asked when you set up PinCam, and changeable any time in Preferences, About). Crash reports contain what went wrong, the phone model, system version and app version. Usage data says which screens and settings are used, how long photos and videos take to save and how long videos are, tied to a random ID for this installation, not to you. Your IP address is used to work out your country. Neither includes your photos, videos, sound, where you took them, addresses or anything you type. Crash reports are kept for 90 days, usage data for 2 months. See firebase.google.com/support/privacy.

Each provider handles this information under its own privacy policy, linked above. We chose them because they protect your information at least as well as this policy does. PinCam shares nothing with anyone else.

When you share a photo or video

When you tap Share, the photo or video goes only to the app or person you pick. Your photos and videos show their location in the stamp and also carry it inside the file (GPS data in its metadata). Keep this in mind before you share them.

What PinCam does not do

  • No accounts or sign in.
  • No crash reports or usage data unless you agree.
  • No ads on the camera, and no ad you didn’t choose to watch, other than the gallery banner.
  • No selling or renting of your information.
  • No location use in the background.
  • No recording in the background: recording stops when PinCam leaves the screen.

How your information is kept safe

PinCam’s copies of your photos and videos, its gallery list and your preferences are kept in PinCam’s private storage on your phone, which other apps cannot open and which your phone’s lock protects. Everything PinCam sends over the internet is encrypted.

Keeping and deleting your information

Everything is kept on your phone until you delete it:

  • Deleting a photo or video in PinCam removes PinCam’s copy and its entry. The copy in your phone’s photo library stays until you delete it there.
  • Uninstalling PinCam deletes all of its storage and preferences. Photos and videos in your photo library stay.
  • You can switch off camera, microphone, location or photo access at any time in your phone’s Settings.
  • You can stop sharing usage data at any time: Preferences, About, Share usage data. Reports not yet sent are deleted.

We hold no information that identifies you. Crash reports and usage data are kept by Firebase for the times above and then deleted. For what the services above keep, see their privacy policies.

Children

PinCam is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect information from anyone, including children.

Changes to this policy

If PinCam starts using information in a new way, we will update this policy and its date before the change reaches you, and mention it in the app’s update notes.

Contact
